01

Overview & quick access

Acme Widget Co. is a three-product storefront with an automatic red-widget offer and delivery pricing. You can experiment freely: there is no payment form and no order is placed.

Where to go Address or location When to use it
Local development storefront localhost:5173 After running pnpm dev.
Local production storefront localhost:8080 After Docker Compose, or a production build started with its asset directory.
Source repository elitecoderdev/acme-widget-co Code, README, tests, deployment files, and API examples.
Cloud application URL returned by your Cloud Run deployment After an operator provisions and verifies a deployment. A live cloud URL is not assumed in this guide.
Postman files docs/postman/ Import the collection and environment to exercise the API.
Before you begin

Ask your operator for the application address, or follow section 08 or 09 to start it locally. No account is required by the storefront. An IAM-protected Cloud Run deployment may require access through your organization's approved entry point.

02

Your first estimate

Shopper walkthrough

Start with one red widget, then add another to see the offer apply automatically. You do not need a promotional code.

1

Open the collection

Open the application address in your browser. Wait for the three product cards to appear. If you are lower on the page, select The collection in the header or Explore the collection in an empty basket.

You should see: Red Widget, Green Widget, and Blue Widget, each with a price and an Add button.

2

Add your first Red Widget

Select Add on the Red Widget card. The basket count becomes 1. The application requests a fresh estimate and briefly displays Updating your estimate… while it waits.

Expected estimate: $32.95 merchandise + $4.95 delivery = $37.90.

3

Add a second Red Widget

Select Add on the same card again, or use the basket row's + control. The quantity becomes 2. A Red pair offer line appears with an Applied label.

Expected estimate: $65.90 subtotal − $16.48 offer + $4.95 delivery = $54.37.

4

Read the result

Review Subtotal, the offer if applicable, Delivery, and Estimated total. All amounts are USD. The delivery progress indicator shows the additional merchandise value needed to reach free delivery after offers.

You are done: This is an estimate. There is no checkout, payment, stock reservation, or order confirmation to complete.

03

Manage your basket

Every quantity change updates the selection immediately and requests a new server-calculated estimate.

1

Increase or decrease a quantity

Use + to add one unit and − to remove one unit from that product row. Reducing a quantity from 1 removes that product from the basket. The amount at the end of each row is its standard unit price multiplied by quantity; the red-pair discount appears in the summary.

2

Remove a product completely

Select the × beside a product's name. This removes all units of that product. The remaining products stay selected and the estimate refreshes.

3

Start again with an empty basket

Select Clear basket below the estimate. All selected products are removed at once. The empty-basket message returns. You can also remove the final product with its × control or decrease its last unit to zero.

Your selection stays only in the open page

The basket is kept in browser memory. Refreshing the page or opening a new application tab starts an empty basket. Browser back navigation may restore the previous page, but the application does not save the basket. There is no account, saved basket, or cross-device synchronization. Use the retry control after an estimate error if you want to retain your current selection.

The 100-unit limit

A basket can contain at most 100 units in total across all products. At that limit, Add and increase controls are disabled and an explanatory message appears. Decrease or remove an item to enable them again. The API also enforces the limit; it is not only a visual restriction.

04

Understand the price

The server combines the catalog, automatic offers, and delivery bands. The browser displays the result; it does not choose the price.

Product Product code Unit price Offer
Red Widget R01 $32.95 Every second red widget is half price.
Green Widget G01 $24.95 Standard unit price.
Blue Widget B01 $7.95 Standard unit price.

How the red-pair offer is rounded

Half of $32.95 is $16.475. Each discounted red widget is rounded down to $16.47. One full-price red widget and one discounted red widget therefore cost $49.42 before delivery. This makes the saving $16.48. The rule is applied separately to each discounted unit: one pair for two reds, one pair for three reds, two pairs for four reds.

Standard-price subtotal · 2 × $32.95$65.90
Red pair offer− $16.48
Merchandise after the offer$49.42
Delivery · merchandise below $50+ $4.95
Estimated total$54.37

Delivery is based on the amount after offers

Discounted merchandise value Delivery Boundary rule
Empty basket $0.00 No merchandise and no delivery charge.
Below $50.00 $4.95 $49.99 is still in this band.
$50.00 to below $90.00 $2.95 Exactly $50.00 enters this band.
$90.00 or more Free Exactly $90.00 qualifies.
Why two red widgets do not get $2.95 delivery

Their undiscounted subtotal is $65.90, but the delivery calculation uses $49.42 after the offer. That is below $50.00, so delivery is $4.95. No tax, payment fee, or additional service charge is modeled by this challenge.

  1. Scroll to A few good combinations.
  2. Select a sample button. Its contents replace your current selection.
  3. Wait for the refreshed estimate and compare it with the total shown on the sample.
  4. Adjust quantities if you want to explore a variation.
Selection After offers Delivery Estimated total
1 Blue + 1 Green $32.90 $4.95 $37.85
2 Red $49.42 $4.95 $54.37
1 Red + 1 Green $57.90 $2.95 $60.85
2 Blue + 3 Red $98.27 Free $98.27
06

Mobile & keyboard use

The same collection and pricing rules are available on a phone. The layout changes to fit the screen.

On a phone

  1. Open the same application URL.
  2. Scroll through the product cards and tap Add.
  3. Once the basket contains an item, use View basket to jump to its position on the page.
  4. Use the basket's +, −, or × controls as you would on desktop.
  5. Scroll back to the collection to choose another product.

With a keyboard

  • Use Tab and Shift + Tab to move between interactive controls.
  • The Skip to content link appears when focused.
  • Activate a focused link with Enter; buttons also support Space.
  • Product-specific control names identify which item changes.
  • Loading, errors, and basket counts use accessible status announcements.

The application uses system fonts and local product illustrations. It does not require an external font service. The manual itself is responsive too: expand Contents & section search near the top to navigate on a small screen.

07

Recover from a problem

A connection problem should not leave you guessing whether a displayed amount belongs to your latest selection.

If the collection does not load

  1. Check that the application server is running and your network connection is available.
  2. On the A small pause. screen, select Reload collection.
  3. Wait for the product cards to return. If the failure repeats, use section 17 or contact the operator.

If an estimate cannot be calculated

  1. Your selected items remain visible.
  2. Check the connection or wait briefly if the service is busy.
  3. Select Try estimate again to resend the current basket.
  4. Read the total only after the updated estimate appears.
Requests have a 10-second timeout

The browser stops waiting after 10 seconds and shows the relevant retry state. That is a maximum wait for one request, not a normal response-time promise. Old requests are cancelled or ignored when a newer selection replaces them. A slow previous result must not overwrite the newest basket.

A very busy instance may return a rate-limit response. Wait about a minute before retrying repeatedly. The application's limit is shared by quote requests on an instance; it is not a personal allowance tied to your account.

08

Run on your computer

Developer setup

You need Git, Node.js, and pnpm. The application does not need a database, a login provider, or a Google Cloud project to run locally.

1. Get the project and pinned tools

Clone the repository and enter its directory. Use the Node version in .node-version—24.21.0 for this guide—and pnpm 11.25.0. Install Node through your usual trusted installer or version manager. 

git clone https://github.com/elitecoderdev/acme-widget-co.git
cd acme-widget-co
node --version
npm install --global pnpm@11.25.0 --ignore-scripts
pnpm --version
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

GitHub may request authentication if your account does not have anonymous access to the repository. Do not place credentials in the clone URL or commit them to the project.

2. Start development mode

pnpm dev

Keep the terminal open. Visit http://localhost:5173. The frontend development server runs on port 5173 and forwards API requests to the backend on port 8080. Edits reload during development. Use Ctrl + C in the terminal to stop the processes.

3. Verify the production build

Run the checks first, then serve the compiled files. The following environment commands use PowerShell: 

pnpm check
$env:NODE_ENV = "production"
$env:HOST = "127.0.0.1"
$env:PORT = "8080"
$env:STATIC_DIR = (Resolve-Path "apps/web/dist").Path
pnpm start

Open http://localhost:8080. The built API now serves the frontend from the same origin. STATIC_DIR must point to a directory containing index.html; startup fails if the configured frontend build is missing.

Development and production use different browser addresses

Use port 5173 with pnpm dev. Use port 8080 with Docker or the production start command above. Opening port 8080 during development may expose only the API, because the frontend is being served separately by Vite.

09

Run with Docker

Docker Compose runs the production package using a single command. On Windows, start Docker Desktop and select Linux containers first.

  1. Open a terminal in the repository root.
  2. Confirm Docker is running with docker info.
  3. Build and start the application:
docker compose up --build --detach --wait

Open http://localhost:8080. Compose waits for the readiness check. The published port binds to the local loopback interface, so this local configuration does not intentionally expose the storefront to the rest of your network.

Task Command
Check running containers docker compose ps
Read recent logs docker compose logs --tail=100 app
Follow logs live docker compose logs --follow app
Stop and remove the local container docker compose down
Rebuild after changing source docker compose up --build --detach --wait

The image has separate build and production-dependency stages. Dependencies are installed from the frozen lockfile. The final application runs as an unprivileged user. Compose adds a read-only filesystem, a small temporary directory, dropped capabilities, and resource limits. These local controls complement Cloud Run's managed container environment; they are not a substitute for cloud access policies.

10

How the solution works

The architecture is a small modular monolith with a hexagonal pricing core. In practical terms, pricing rules are separate from the website, HTTP server, and cloud platform.

  1. 1. React storefrontThe shopper changes product quantities.
  2. 2. Fastify APIThe server validates the submitted basket.
  3. 3. Pricing coreCatalog, offer, and delivery policies calculate integer cents.
  4. 4. Estimate displayThe browser presents the returned amounts.
Module Responsibility Useful files
packages/domain Basket rules, immutable catalog values, integer money, offers, delivery, and domain errors. basket.ts, offers.ts, delivery.ts, money.ts, defaults.ts
apps/api Input/output schemas, HTTP endpoints, security headers, rate limiting, health checks, application lifecycle, and static assets. src/application/quote-basket.ts, src/http/app.ts, src/http/schemas.ts
apps/web Accessible product selection, quantity controls, loading/retry states, and currency presentation. src/App.tsx, src/useStore.ts, src/api.ts, src/styles.css
infra/terraform Artifact Registry, Cloud Run, runtime identity, scaling, health probes, and access configuration. main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf

Why these boundaries matter

A new offer or delivery policy can be supplied to the pricing core without embedding its rules in an HTTP route or React component. Each part has one clear responsibility. Small policy contracts support dependency inversion and substitution; shared types and calculations reduce duplication. No dependency injection framework is necessary for this scope.

Vite builds the frontend and the Node server. Domain code is inlined into the compiled server bundle, while Fastify dependencies remain separate runtime packages. The deployment preserves pnpm's workspace links and uses one origin for browser assets and API calls.

Why there is no database

Each estimate is calculated from the submitted basket and versioned pricing configuration. There is nothing durable to store for the challenge. Adding real checkout would require a separate design for orders, inventory, accepted price versions, payments, authentication, and durable records. The current quote endpoint must not be treated as an order-creation API.

11

API reference

The local API base address is http://localhost:8080. All monetary response fields use integer cents. Divide by 100 only when presenting an amount.

Method & path Purpose Successful result
GET /api/catalog Read products, delivery rules, offer details, and sample basket definitions with their prices. 200 JSON catalog.
POST /api/quotes Calculate the supplied basket. 200 JSON quote.
GET /healthz Check process liveness. 200 with status ok.
GET /readyz Check startup/readiness. 200 with status ready.

Example request: two red widgets

Send Content-Type: application/json with the following body:

{
  "items": [
    { "code": "R01", "quantity": 2 }
  ]
}

Read the response

Field Meaning Two-red example
currency Currency code. USD
itemCount Total product units. 2
subtotalCents All units at standard prices. 6590
discountCents Saving from the red-pair offer. 1648
merchandiseCents Subtotal after offers. 4942
deliveryCents Delivery charge. 495
totalCents Merchandise plus delivery. 5437
freeDeliveryRemainingCents Merchandise value still needed for $90 free-delivery threshold. 4058
items Per-product quantities, standard prices, subtotal, discount, and total. One row for R01.

An empty request basket, {"items":[]}, returns zero merchandise, delivery, and total. The server rejects unsupported product codes, negative or fractional quantities, unknown request fields, and baskets exceeding the limit. Request bodies are bounded to 16 KiB.

Status What it means What to do
400 Invalid shape, quantity, or field. Send only the documented fields with whole-number quantities.
404 Unknown endpoint. Check the method and path.
413 Body exceeds the size limit. Send a bounded basket.
415 Unsupported content type. Use application/json.
422 Domain rule rejects the basket. Check product codes and total quantity.
429 Instance quote allowance exhausted. Wait and retry; inspect rate metrics if persistent.
500 Unexpected server failure. Retry once, then inspect operator logs.
12

Use the Postman collection

Postman lets you inspect requests and responses without using the storefront. The repository's collection and local environment are under docs/postman/.

  1. Start the application with development mode, a production build, or Docker. Confirm localhost:8080/healthz responds.
  2. Open Postman and select Import.
  3. Select Acme-Widget-Co.postman_collection.json and Acme-Widget-Co-Local.postman_environment.json from docs/postman/.
  4. Select Acme Widget Co - Local in Postman's environment selector.
  5. Confirm its baseUrl variable is http://localhost:8080. Keep the protocol and port; do not append /api. Each request already supplies its endpoint path.
  6. Send the health and catalog requests first.
  7. Send the quote examples. Compare their totals with section 05.
  8. Run the collection to execute its included assertions, and inspect any failed response before changing application code.

Manual fallback request

If you prefer to create a request yourself, choose POST, enter http://localhost:8080/api/quotes, select Body → raw → JSON, and paste the two-red request from section 11. Select Send and confirm totalCents is 5437.

Use the correct environment

A local collection calls your computer, not a cloud instance. To test a deployed service, duplicate the environment and replace its base URL with the exact Cloud Run or approved gateway URL. An IAM-protected service also needs the approved caller authentication. Never commit tokens or personal environment values.

13

Tests & quality checks

The project combines business-rule tests, API tests, UI tests, browser journeys, and production packaging checks. Coverage is a gate, not a substitute for correct assertions.

95%Enforced minimum in each coverage metric
209Unit/integration tests in the recorded validation snapshot
100%Recorded source coverage snapshot
4Required challenge baskets checked end to end

Recorded figures describe the verification run used to prepare this guide. Re-run the commands below after any change; the generated reports and CI results are authoritative for the current commit. Terraform and container configuration are checked separately and are not part of source-code line coverage.

Recorded local verification

Check Recorded result Interpretation
Unit and integration suite 209 tests passed; 100% source coverage. The checked source exceeded all four 95% coverage gates.
Local security checks 44 checks passed. These checks exercise the implemented controls; they are not a comprehensive penetration test.
Local request burst 400 requests; measured p95 latency of 22 ms. A short local burst measurement, not a sustained load test, cloud benchmark, or production capacity guarantee.
Automated Playwright journeys Execution pending because of local environment restrictions. The suite is provided; this recorded snapshot does not claim it passed.
Docker build and container checks Execution pending because of local environment restrictions. The image and Compose configuration still require an actual build and container run in a working Docker environment.
Command What it proves
pnpm typecheck TypeScript contracts are consistent across packages.
pnpm test Domain, API, and component behavior.
pnpm test:coverage Tests plus the 95% statements, branches, functions, and lines gates.
pnpm check Type checking, coverage tests, and production builds together.
pnpm test:e2e Desktop and mobile browser journeys using the compiled application.
pnpm audit --audit-level=high Current package advisories at high or critical severity.

Run the full local verification

pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm check
pnpm exec playwright install chromium
pnpm test:e2e
pnpm audit --audit-level=high

On a Linux machine missing browser system libraries, use pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium with the operating-system permissions required for those libraries. Coverage HTML is written under coverage/; browser reports are under playwright-report/. Open the generated report to inspect failures instead of relying only on a percentage.

What the test layers cover

  • Domain: exact reference totals, half-price rounding, delivery boundaries, invalid inputs, limits, and replaceable policies.
  • API: JSON contracts, rejected requests, security-related responses, health routes, static files, and safe failure handling.
  • UI: add/remove/quantity controls, empty and error states, retries, examples, delivery feedback, and accessibility-relevant behavior.
  • Browser and container: real navigation, mobile layout, compiled assets, quote calculations, and production startup.

GitHub Actions runs the repository checks with pinned action revisions and minimal repository permissions. A green code-test job alone does not establish that the container or infrastructure jobs passed; inspect the complete workflow before release.

14

Prepare a GCP deployment

Operator workflow

The repository includes a Cloud Run deployment configuration. This section describes how to use it; it does not claim that resources have already been created in your Google Cloud project.

Resource Purpose
Artifact Registry Stores versioned application container images.
Cloud Run Runs the stateless storefront/API container and terminates HTTPS.
Runtime service account Identifies the running application; it has no project roles by default.
Startup and liveness probes Check readiness on /readyz and health on /healthz.
  1. Choose a project and region. Billing must be enabled. Use an approved deployment identity and install Google Cloud CLI, Docker, and the Terraform version documented in docs/deployment.md.
  2. Prepare Terraform state. Use a private, versioned GCS backend for shared or production operations. Do not commit state files or private variable files.
  3. Bootstrap the registry and identity. With deploy_service=false, review and apply the Terraform plan. This creates prerequisites without deploying a placeholder application.
  4. Build a verified release. Run the quality checks, build a Linux image from the selected commit, tag it, and push it to Artifact Registry.
  5. Resolve its immutable digest. Use an image reference ending in @sha256:…. Terraform rejects a tag-only application image.
  6. Choose access deliberately. Keep public_access=false for IAM protection. Use true only when this anonymous quote website is intended to be public.
  7. Deploy the service. Set deploy_service=true and the digest, review the plan, and apply it.
  8. Verify the result. Read service_url, check readiness, open the storefront, and repeat the four challenge baskets.
Use the detailed runbook for exact commands

docs/deployment.md provides the PowerShell bootstrap, build, push, digest, and apply commands. Read the plan before applying: deployment creates billable resources. No cloud credentials belong in the repository or this manual.

Default capacity settings

The Terraform starting configuration uses one CPU, 512 MiB memory, 80 concurrent requests per instance, zero minimum instances, and a maximum of 20 instances. These are configuration limits, not measured throughput or availability claims. Scale-to-zero can introduce startup latency after inactivity. Tune capacity from representative tests and cost requirements.

What is outside the base module

The base configuration does not create a custom domain, external HTTP load balancer, Cloud Armor policy, global per-client quota, order database, or payment service. Client-aware edge controls require additional infrastructure. The fixed instance rate limit is documented in the next section.

15

Security & safe configuration

The browser is untrusted. The API selects prices, validates quantities, and calculates the final quote from its own policies.

For a shopper

  • No account, payment card, or address is needed for a quote.
  • Use the correct application URL.
  • Use HTTPS for a real remote deployment.
  • Do not enter personal data into developer tools or undocumented request fields.

For an operator

  • Keep runtime and deployment identities separate.
  • Use short-lived authentication for automated delivery.
  • Store future secrets in an approved secret manager.
  • Review dependency updates and image advisories.
  • Restrict log and Terraform-state access to operators.

Environment variables

Variable Use Example
NODE_ENV Production runtime mode. production
HOST Listen interface. Use loopback for a manual local run and all interfaces inside the container. 127.0.0.1 locally; 0.0.0.0 in the image.
PORT HTTP listen port. Cloud Run supplies it. 8080
STATIC_DIR Directory containing the compiled storefront. /app/apps/web/dist in the image.

These are runtime settings, not secrets. The current application needs no secret to calculate quotes. Do not add service-account keys, access tokens, private environment files, or personal Postman values to Git. Keep the committed lockfile and install with --frozen-lockfile; pnpm improves repeatability but does not automatically make every dependency trustworthy.

Understand the instance rate limit

Only POST /api/quotes consumes the allowance: 1,000 requests per minute per instance, using the fixed key instance. Catalog, asset, and health requests do not consume that quote bucket. The application does not trust forwarded client-IP headers for quota selection, so changing X-Forwarded-For does not provide a new bucket.

The allowance is shared by visitors handled by that process and increases across replicas. It is not a global or personal quota. Use Cloud Armor with an external HTTP load balancer when client-aware edge limits are required; neither resource is provisioned by the base Terraform module. Set budget alerts as well: instance limits are not hard billing limits.

Production responses use browser security headers, including a Content Security Policy. The storefront and API share one origin. Do not add broad CORS permissions or weaken security headers to hide a configuration error.

16

Maintain the application

A release is a tested commit and an identifiable image. Keep both recorded so a previous version can be restored deliberately.

Routine Action
Before release Run checks, inspect CI, review dependency/image advisories, and record the commit and image digest.
After release Check readiness, open the page, verify sample totals, and observe errors and latency.
During operation Watch request count, 4xx/5xx and 429 rates, latency, CPU, memory, instance count, and startup failures.
Dependency maintenance Review proposed updates and lockfile changes. Re-run tests and rebuild the image.
Artifact cleanup Retain the current release and a known working rollback image before removing older images.

If a release must be rolled back

Reapply the desired Terraform configuration using the previous successful image digest and the correct environment values. Verify the storefront and reference baskets afterward. An emergency traffic change through the Cloud Run CLI must later be reconciled with Terraform so the next apply does not undo the incident response.

Keep logs useful

Read recent container logs locally with docker compose logs --tail=100 app. For a Cloud Run deployment, use the service's logs in Google Cloud or the documented CLI commands. Do not add request bodies, future customer details, tokens, or secrets to diagnostic output.

Remove an environment carefully

Cloud Run deletion protection is enabled by default. Disabling it and destroying an environment removes availability and can remove stored artifacts. Review the Terraform plan and project before any destructive operation. Quote data does not need a backup, but Terraform state and deployment records do.

17

Troubleshooting reference

Start with the symptom. Correct the underlying configuration before repeatedly restarting or changing dependencies.

Symptom Likely explanation Next step
The browser cannot connect The server is stopped or the wrong port is open. Check the terminal or Compose status. Use 5173 for development and 8080 for production.
Collection fails to load The frontend is available but the API request failed. Check API health and the dev proxy, then select Reload collection.
Estimate fails or times out The service is unavailable, busy, or exceeded the 10-second request wait. Keep the page open, check connectivity, and select Try estimate again.
Expected items disappeared The page was refreshed, opened in a new tab, or replaced by a sample basket. Recreate the selection. Basket persistence is outside this application's scope.
Add or + is disabled The basket already contains 100 units. Decrease or remove an item first.
Delivery differs from the raw subtotal Delivery uses the subtotal after offers. Compare merchandise after discounts with the $50 and $90 thresholds.
Port is already in use Another development or production process is running. Stop the old process or choose another API port and update the corresponding frontend/API configuration.
Production startup reports missing index.html The frontend has not been built or STATIC_DIR is wrong. Run pnpm build and point STATIC_DIR to apps/web/dist.
Frozen install rejects the lockfile Manifest and lockfile versions no longer match. Restore the matching files from the intended commit, or intentionally regenerate/review the lockfile as a dependency change.
Docker reports a daemon/engine error Docker Desktop is stopped, using the wrong container mode, or blocked by host permissions. Start the Linux engine and verify docker info. Resolve host permissions through normal administration.
Browser tests cannot launch Chromium The browser package or OS dependencies are missing. Install the Playwright browser; on Linux include required system dependencies.
Cloud URL returns an access error The service is private or organization policies restrict public access. Use the approved authenticated entry point or review the invoker policy.
Quote requests return 429 The shared instance quote allowance has been reached. Wait before retrying; an operator should review load and rate metrics if it persists.
Unexpected 500 responses The server encountered an unhandled failure. Record the time and active revision, inspect logs, and use the rollback runbook if a release introduced it.

When reporting a problem, include the application address, browser, steps, approximate time, observed message, and expected result. Include the commit or deployment revision if you know it. Exclude credentials and other sensitive information.

18

Handover & reference

Use this final checklist to confirm that a reviewer or operator can reproduce the intended experience.

  • The storefront opens at the documented local or deployment URL.
  • All three products display the correct code and unit price.
  • Adding, decreasing, removing, clearing, and sample replacement work.
  • The four sample totals match $37.85, $54.37, $60.85, and $98.27.
  • Loading and retry states remain understandable; a quote error preserves the selection.
  • The phone layout exposes View basket for a nonempty basket.
  • The current commit passes quality gates and the relevant browser/container checks.
  • Postman uses the intended environment and returns the reference totals.
  • A cloud release, if performed, records its project, region, image digest, access policy, and rollback candidate.
